symptom: `describe java action GenAICommons.ChunkCollection_AddKnowledgeBaseChunk` printed `MxObject: "Entity"` with nothing declaring the type parameter Entity; `check` passed, and exec wrote the parameter as the entity `.Entity` — mx check CE1613 "The selected entity '.Entity' no longer exists" (mendixlabs/mxcli#1404).
cause: MDL declared a Java action type parameter only through an `entity <T>` parameter (the visitor collected TypeParameters from those alone), so a type parameter bound by its argument with no entity selector had no spelling. exec then sent the unqualified name down the entity path as Module "" + "." + Name, and no check looked at unqualified type names in a java action signature.
file: mdl/grammar/domains/MDLMicroflow.g4 (javaActionTypeParameters header); mdl/visitor/visitor_javaaction.go (header names first, then entity selectors); mdl/executor/cmd_javaactions.go (javaActionTypeParameterHeader in describe, undeclaredJavaActionTypeNames refusal in exec); mdl/executor/validate_javaaction_types.go (MDL-JA01 at check)
insight: The header is printed only when the entity selectors would not reproduce the stored list in its order, so every action that already round-tripped describes byte-identically. The refusal is the other half: an unqualified type in a java action signature can only be a type parameter or `Microflow`/`Nanoflow` (mapped by exec), so anything else was always a CE1613 that check could have caught. An unbound entity selector (`entity <>`) still has no MDL form; as for JavaScript actions it is commented out under `-- NOT re-executable:`. JavaScript actions keep the commented-out form for the undeclared shape — the header is not in their grammar yet.
